name: SAVE-U
aliases: Sacrospinous fixation versus vaginal hysterectomy in treatment of uterine prolapse >=2
question: Is vaginal sacrospinous hysteropexy noninferior to vaginal hysterectomy with uterosacral ligament suspension for apical failure in women with stage 2 or higher uterine prolapse?

arms.label: vaginal hysterectomy with uterosacral ligament suspension

design.population: 208 women with POP-Q stage 2 or higher uterine prolapse needing surgery and no previous pelvic floor surgery, in four Dutch non-university teaching hospitals.

verdictNote: Noninferiority margin of 7 percentage points met; 0/102 versus 4/100 apical failures at 12 months.
takeaway: In women with stage 2 or higher uterine prolapse, vaginal sacrospinous hysteropexy was noninferior to vaginal hysterectomy with uterosacral ligament suspension for apical failure with bothersome bulge or repeat surgery at 12 months (0/102 versus 4/100; difference -3.9 points, 95% CI -8.6 to 0.7).

reports.label: 12-month randomized report
reports.citation: Detollenaere RJ, den Boon J, Stekelenburg J, et al. Sacrospinous hysteropexy versus vaginal hysterectomy with suspension of the uterosacral ligaments in women with uterine prolapse stage 2 or higher: multicentre randomised non-inferiority trial. *BMJ.* 2015;351:h3717. doi:10.1136/bmj.h3717
reports.followUp: 12 months; independent examiner not involved in treatment

results.measure: 12-month apical-compartment surgical failure (POP-Q stage 2 or higher of uterus or vault with bothersome bulge symptoms, or repeat surgery for apical prolapse); intention to treat with last observation carried forward; risk difference in percentage points (hysteropexy minus hysterectomy)
results.note: Prespecified noninferiority margin 7 percentage points; upper confidence limit 0.7. Conservative imputation (failure for missing data): 6/103 (6%) versus 10/105 (10%), difference -3.6 (95% CI -11.2 to 3.9). Per protocol: 0/98 (0%) versus 3/90 (3%), difference -3.3 (95% CI -8.0 to 1.3).

results.note: More posterior colporrhaphies were performed with hysterectomy (52/105, 50%) than with hysteropexy (30/103, 29%).

PISQ-12 total score at 12 months, mean (SD)
results.note: Scores improved from baseline in both groups (P<0.002 each); baseline 33 (6) and 35 (5).

harms.label: Buttock pain during hospital stay
harms.note: Resolved spontaneously within 6 weeks in 8 of 9 women (VAS below 2). One woman had suture cutting and vaginal hysterectomy at 4 months for persistent pain at the suture site.

harms.label: Urinary retention (more than 150 mL after catheter removal)
harms.note: Managed with a transurethral catheter or clean intermittent self-catheterization; spontaneous voiding returned in all women after a median of 5 days of catheterization (range 1 to 40).

harms.label: Serious adverse events during hospital stay
harms.note: None judged related to the type of surgery. Hysteropexy group: stroke with full recovery, postoperative pneumonia, anaphylaxis to prophylactic antibiotics. Hysterectomy group: atrial fibrillation requiring cardioversion, and one death from paralytic ileus, aspiration pneumonia and multi-organ failure.

harms.label: Hysterectomy after hysteropexy by 12 months
harms.note: One for persistent buttock pain (at 4 months) and one for endometrial carcinoma found during follow-up.

harms.label: Subsequent stress incontinence surgery after 12 months

delivery.label: Technique, hysteropexy
delivery.value: Right sacrospinous ligament; two permanent sutures (Prolene 1.0) under direct vision at least 2 cm from the ischial spine, then through the posterior cervix.
delivery.note: Posterior vaginal wall incision and access through the pararectal space; posterior wall closed with absorbable suture.

delivery.label: Technique, hysterectomy
delivery.value: Vaginal hysterectomy; uterosacral ligaments ligated and transected, then attached to the vaginal vault.
delivery.note: McCall culdoplasty was used instead of uterosacral suspension in 6/102 (6%) of the hysterectomy group.

delivery.label: Procedures performed by residents under supervision
delivery.note: Overall surgical failure did not differ by gynecologist or resident (91/180 versus 9/19, P=0.81).

delivery.label: Crossover and deviations
delivery.value: Two women allocated to hysterectomy received hysteropexy for technical difficulty; one had an abdominal hysterectomy for adhesions.
delivery.note: Fourteen protocol deviations in total; all women analyzed as randomized.
